reason: E1 shows that an MTP achieves near-DFT accuracy for energies and forces in a refractory high-entropy alloy, supporting the first premise. However, none of the cited evidence addresses active learning, free-energy calculations, vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, electron–vibration coupling, or computational cost comparisons for fusion-relevant thermodynamics. E2 is about CALPHAD modeling and E3 discusses entropy contributions from DFT but does not involve MLIPs. Thus, most key premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can achieve near-DFT accuracy for energies and forces in multicomponent refractory alloys
Active learning can efficiently target key regions of phase space for training MLIPs
MLIPs can capture vibrational entropy and anharmonicity in solid and liquid phases
MLIPs can capture electron–vibration coupling effects
MLIPs can substantially reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio MD and TOR-TILD for free-energy calculations
